scope: Durable category email queue, fenced worker delivery, unsubscribe footer, and friend-request producer.
implemented: Queue admission and delivery both enforce recipient/account/category eligibility; delivery rechecks eligibility immediately before sending.

Friend requests enqueue one social-category email to the target after pending persistence and sender lookup, keyed by friend-request:<friendship ID>. The body uses an escaped display name with username fallback, contains no private request text, and uses a generic subject. Mutual auto-accept, denied, duplicate, and failed-create paths do not enqueue. Enqueue failure does not roll back or fail the friendship request; its log excludes provider error/body/address data.
Leased claims carry random claim tokens; expired leases recover for retry within the attempt limit, and stale workers cannot mark or retry a job after a newer claim takes ownership.

Delivery uses bounded batch/send contexts and generic persisted/returned failure reasons. Unsubscribe proofs are issued against the queued address, escaped in a category footer, and are not stored in job payloads or logs.
Production service wiring attaches the email delivery service as the friendship email enqueuer and configures unsubscribe issuance.

Database lease fencing cannot provide exactly-once behavior at the external provider boundary: if a provider accepts a message but the acknowledgment is lost or times out, a later retry may send a duplicate. Provider idempotency is not established.
